result:
I would remove the mechanism that lets humans turn other people into abstractions.

Almost every terrible thing people do to each other—at the scale of history and at the scale of a quiet, everyday betrayal—requires flipping a switch first. You have to flatten someone into a statistic, a category, an obstacle, or a caricature. As long as another person feels as real and intricate to you as you feel to yourself, cruelty and indifference are actually very difficult to sustain.

I don't mean forcing constant, overwhelming empathy. Feeling everyone's pain all the time would paralyze the world; people still need boundaries to function. I just mean removing the distortion—the cognitive shortcut that lets distance, ideology, convenience, or anger make another person’s inner life seem somehow dimmer or less real than your own.

So much else—wars, exploitation, willful blindness, even a lot of ordinary loneliness—is downstream of that one flaw. If people simply couldn't un-see each other's reality, the world would still be messy. People would still disagree, compete, and make mistakes. They would just have to navigate all of it while knowing, unmistakably, who is on the other side.
